content.text: The evidence clearly shows io-pay (third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd) returning 503 errors starting exactly at the onset, with cpu_limit_cores holding steady at 3.0 throughout (ruling out autoscaling-pathology), and no deploys in the lookback window that could explain it.

hypotheses.subject: api.io-pay.example
hypotheses.summary: io-shop's account page depends on api.io-pay.example (IO Payments Ltd, third-party) to fetch card details. Starting at 07:33:00Z, io-pay began returning HTTP 503 for every request, which io-shop surfaces as PaymentProviderFailed errors, driving the error rate from baseline (~1%) to 100%. The failure arrived through this dependency; io-shop's own code, config and deployment history show no relevant change.

supporting_evidence.claim: account page request failed - PaymentProviderFailed: api.io-pay.example returned 503 for /v1/shoppers/shopper-64320-11-0/card at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:95
account page error rate at 100.00% over the last minute
io-pay: third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd, at api.io-pay.example - Holds the card Io charges. Called while the account page renders
cpu_limit_cores holds steady at 3.0 across the entire window, including the incident minutes (07:33-07:38), ruling out autoscaling-pathology or capacity change as the cause
No deploys/changes found in the 2026-09-27T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-28T07:38:17Z window that coincide with or precede the onset (per earlier read)
